summary: Code review PASS for WP-003 (Build Verification & Regression Testing). WP-003 is a verification-only work package — no net-new code was introduced. The review scope covers the upstream code changes from WP-001 and WP-002, both landing in scripts/build-personas.js, which were verified to be correct by the Developer and QA pipelines.

WP-001 (default-to-all + info note): SUITE_ARG default change from 'ledger' to 'all' is a clean, single-token edit with no side-effects. The [info] log is placed after the suite-parsing block, matching the --target flag pattern above it — idiomatic and consistent. Header comment correctly documents the new default. Inline comment updated to say '(default: all)'.

WP-002 (ccFrontmatterFields() helper + ccModel comment): The extraction of three shared CC frontmatter fields into a pure zero-parameter helper function is a textbook DRY refactor. JSDoc contract explicitly states 'no leading/trailing newline', which is necessary for correct template interpolation. Interpolation placement within both FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_CC and FRONTMATTER_STANDALONE_CC is correct — the helper output slots cleanly at the ${ccFrontmatterFields()} site with no whitespace artifacts. The ccModel ternary comment is accurate, concise, and preserves forward-compatibility intent.

All four review dimensions are satisfied: (1) Maintainability — minimal diffs, descriptive naming, no complexity creep; (2) Best Practices — DRY applied correctly, validation guards intact, JSDoc style consistent with file conventions; (3) Security/Performance — pure string functions, no I/O or security surface; (4) Future Context — escape hatch is documented, default change is aligned with contributor expectations. One low-priority non-blocking observation recorded (see comments).

comments.note: scripts/build-personas.js — ccFrontmatterFields() is currently monomorphic: it returns the same three fields (permissionMode, model, memory) regardless of suite context. If ledger and standalone CC frontmatter ever diverge (e.g., standalone requires a different permissionMode default, or a fourth field is ledger-only), the helper will need to be split or parameterized. Not a blocker today — the plan explicitly scopes this to three shared fields and the current usage is correct — but worth a comment in the helper's JSDoc if the suite divergence risk ever concretises.

No other observations — both changes are clean and consistent. The SUITE_ARG default flip is the minimal correct change; the --suite validation guards were verified by QA to be intact. The ccFrontmatterFields() refactor produces byte-identical output confirmed by git diff. Overall this is well-structured, incremental work with no regressions.
